purpose: Shaman re-run at 512, conditioned on a render of the front-textured mesh. Its 384 photo-conditioned run failed the structural gate on exactly the front and rear views, at IoU 0.677 and 0.705.

mesh_provenance.decimation: open3d quadric -> 400,000 faces, 6.3 s, watertight, 29 shells
mesh_provenance.front_texture: fast_texture_projection at 2048 from the original 4K transparent PNG; camera IoU 0.876, 400,659 observed texels (22.7% of owned)
mesh_provenance.orientation: Y 178.33 deg from the projection camera, then X +90 into the builder's Z-up basis

camera_semantics.note: silhouette IoU chose the MIRROR profile here (0.881 vs 0.618) because a whale in profile looks nearly the same from port and starboard. The chosen front control saw 5 painted texels of 31,537; the opposite view saw 25,107.

primary.conditioning_note: a render of the textured mesh through the front control camera, not the source photo

oom_fallback.note: No 256 controls were built for this asset. A fallback would need its own control tensor and camera contract, so there is nothing to fall back to; an OOM here is a hard stop, not a retry.

prompt: high quality clean albedo reference of the same antlered bird-skull shaman, layered weathered cloth robes, bone staff with hanging pendants and charms, consistent materials, consistent identity, flat neutral lighting

repair_proofs.note: Both are hardware defects of this GTX 1660 SUPER, not asset-specific, so they carry over unchanged.

canonical_orientation.evidence: build_mvadapter_cpu_controls.py hardcodes world_up=[0,0,1]. The Y-up glTF build produced four horizontal views of a figure lying down, with the standing views landing in the top/bottom slots. Pre-rotating into Z-up fixed it; verified on the normal contact sheet.
